summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, calciphylaxis, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for fever and worsening kidney function. He had recently been treated for necrotizing fasciitis and was on multiple medications, including immunosuppressants. Upon admission, his fever resolved without evidence of infection, and blood cultures were negative. His elevated creatinine was attributed to dehydration and chronic kidney damage from hypertension and vascular disease, confirmed by a kidney biopsy showing glomerulosclerosis and arteriosclerosis without rejection. Blood pressure was initially severe but improved with optimization of antihypertensives, including increasing the clonidine patch and holding nephrotoxic agents. The left leg wound showed granulation tissue but persistent tendon exposure, prompting outpatient plastic surgery follow-up. Wound care was transitioned to wet-to-dry dressings. Pain medications were adjusted for renal function, and he was discharged home with home health services and close follow-up planned.
